summary: The dual-majority receipt (79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8) reproduced every predicted observation: the silently created two-server change {A,B,C}->{A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2, entry index 11, A commit 11, E holding the same configuration entry, B still at index 10), the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A still led in term 3 (index 3), and after healing A's entry 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 — the committed configuration entry truncated on the node that committed it (index 4). Both comparisons were scored unknown because my declared identity field was missing from the result events, so I fixed the harness to emit the entry index in both result events and submitted it as a successor experiment with previous_id/revision_reason for fresh execution. The interpretation now cites all six receipts, marks the disjoint-majority gap resolved, and adds the retained fact that a configuration entry inside the replayed committed prefix is never restored from the log; the unscored comparison status is recorded honestly as a limitation rather than as evidence.
